title: Orion - Incident Postmortem & Next Steps
summary: Postmortem review for 2027-07-20 production outage impacting inference latency for Orion Health. Covered timeline, root cause (KV cache pressure + autoscaler misconfiguration), immediate mitigations applied, and long-term reliability improvements. Agreed on a set of action items and a follow-up benchmarking run next week.
topics: Root cause analysis (KV cache pressure + autoscaler)
transcript: 00:00 - Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I know this is a follow-up to the outage on the 20th. we want to be concise and make sure next steps are clear. 00:18 - Lena Ortiz: Thanks, Ava. we lost a chunk of traffic between 02:14 and 02:40 UTC, latencies spiked to 6-8s and some requests timed out, causing user-facing failures. 00:36 - Samir Patel: Right, our initial dive showed KV cache thrash - prefix cache eviction under load - combined with the horizontal autoscaler not kicking in quickly because CPU thresholds were on a 5m average. 00:58 - Marcus Reed: Can you say that again, samir? CPU average threshold caused it to not scale fast enough? 01:05 - Samir Patel: yeah, basically the scale policy was smoothing out short spikes; the workload had bursty long-context requests that killed the cache and produced extra GPU work. 01:20 - Priya Kumar: We also saw increased token counts on a specific route which we hadn't accounted for, that route uses a custom prompt pipeline. 01:32 - Ava Chen: So root cause summary: KV cache pressure causing unexpected cache misses + scale policy too slow = latency storm. we pushed a mitigation - disabled aggressive prefix eviction and temporarily increased min replicas. 01:49 - Lena Ortiz: That helped, we saw latencies drop back to normal in about 8-10 minutes. 02:00 - Samir Patel: We also rolled a fallback to a lower-context model variant for that route so token compute dropped by ~40% during the incident. 02:10 - Marcus Reed: Is that fallback behavior something we can control from our side or does Redwood need to configure? 02:18 - Ava Chen: You can opt into automatic fallback in routing policies; we can also set per-route overrides. we'll send the config snippet. 02:30 - Priya Kumar: Quick question about logs - we need full kernel/call traces for the 02:14 window, are those available? 02:38 - Samir Patel: yes we've exported runtime traces and kv-miss metrics, we'll upload to the secure link. 02:45 - Lena Ortiz: Also want to confirm this doesn't have data-residency or encryption implications - anything copied out of VPC? 02:55 - Ava Chen: No, all artifacts were from your Dedicated pool; nothing left the VPC. logs are scrubbed and access-controlled via the shared S3 with your KMS key. 03:10 - Marcus Reed: Ok good. on compliance: does this require us to notify anyone externally? 03:16 - Ava Chen: From a SOC2 perspective it's an operational incident; we recommend internal tracking and we can provide the audit log export. If you need a formal incident report for your board I can help format one. 03:30 - Priya Kumar: Thanks, that would help. 03:35 - Samir Patel: Long-term fixes: tweak autoscaler policy (shorter windows for bursty loads), improve KV cache eviction policy, introduce per-route token budgeting and warning alerts, and add an internal canary that exercises the long-context route. 03:52 - Lena Ortiz: Can you explain per-route token budgeting? 03:57 - Samir Patel: it's a limit on token-in-flight for a route; if it goes over a threshold we can queue or route to the fallback model, avoiding cache thrash. 04:10 - Marcus Reed: Any concerns about quality when we route to the lower-context variant? 04:16 - Ava Chen: Slight drop in fidelity for very long prompts, but for your majority of queries the difference is negligible. We'll attach example outputs. 04:26 - Priya Kumar: timeline for the fixes? 04:30 - Samir Patel: immediate: autoscaler tweak and per-route fallback config (today/within 24h). short term (1-2 weeks): implement token budgeting + improved cache heuristics. medium term (4-8 weeks): telemetry-based model selection and a canary harness. 04:47 - Lena Ortiz: ok. also we want to run a benchmark that simulates the 20th traffic profile - can Redwood run that with our test keys? 04:56 - Ava Chen: yes we'll coordinate a replay; need your traffic sample and a time window. we'll run on dedicated test pool to avoid impacting production. 05:06 - Marcus Reed: we'll share sample traces by EOD. 05:10 - Priya Kumar: Security question: were any customer keys shipped? 05:14 - Ava Chen: No, keys stayed with your KMS; logs are accessible by the list of IAM principals you specified. 05:22 - Lena Ortiz: Are there any config changes that we need to review because they touch RBAC? 05:28 - Ava Chen: we'll include the exact policy changes as a PR to your infra repo so you can review. 05:34 - Samir Patel: A note on monitoring - we recommend adding a KV-miss rate alert and a steep latency tail SLO alert at p99.9; that would catch this class earlier. 05:47 - Lena Ortiz: Good call. 05:50 - Marcus Reed: Competitor wise - our infra team asked why we didn't just move to a self-hosted runtime, citing cost. any comment? 05:58 - Ava Chen: Self-hosting trades off control for maintenance. For Orion's compliance needs, Redwood Private or Dedicated gives the same control with the operational SLA and audit support; we'll share a cost/perf comparison sheet. 06:15 - Priya Kumar: we also discussed capacity - do you recommend increasing baseline reserved GPUs? 06:20 - Samir Patel: Not necessarily, smarter routing and token budgets often solves before adding hardware. but if your growth ramps up, reserved capacity helps stabilize tail latencies. 06:33 - Ava Chen: ok to recap next steps, I'm going to list them and check we all agree. 06:40 - Ava Chen: 1) Redwood to share incident timeline, traces, and security audit artifacts (by 2027-07-23). 06:48 - Lena Ortiz: got it. 06:50 - Ava Chen: 2) Redwood to push autoscaler policy tweak & fallback config to Orion test cluster (within 24h). 06:58 - Marcus Reed: fine. 07:00 - Ava Chen: 3) Orion to provide traffic sample and perf traces (by EOD 2027-07-22). 07:07 - Priya Kumar: we'll do that. 07:10 - Ava Chen: 4) Redwood will run benchmark replay on dedicated test pool and share results (target 2027-07-28). 07:20 - Lena Ortiz: and 5) schedule follow-up in one week to review benchmark and action-item progress. 07:28 - Ava Chen: thanks everyone, we'll send the meeting notes, configs, and a short postmortem doc. 07:35 - Marcus Reed: thanks, appreciate the quick response. 07:38 - Lena Ortiz: thanks all. 07:40 - (call ends)
